name: 01_reset
title: Reset: asynchronous assertion, release after two clocks
explanation: KEY=2 means KEY0 is held low while KEY1 is released. KEY becomes 3 at 120 ns; reset_sync progresses 0 → 1 → 3 at 130/150 ns. rst_n releases at 150 ns, after two rising edges. TX is idle high; permit and error_code remain zero. This prevents a false E-stop at a clean boot.

name: 02_rx_exact_bits
title: RX: exact 0x5A, LSB first, 8N1
explanation: Read the named sample markers left to right: start 0; data D0..D7 = 0,1,0,1,1,0,1,0; stop 1. That is 0x5A. Each bit lasts 54 × 20 ns = 1080 ns. The receiver validates the start at half a bit, samples data once per bit, and pulses valid only after a high stop bit. data becomes 5A; error stays 0.

name: 03_rx_synchronizer
title: RX clock crossing: two sampled registers
explanation: The falling RX edge is followed by meta and then sync on successive 50 MHz rising edges. The state machine reads sync, not the asynchronous pin. This is the intended synchronizer structure; a digital RTL simulation does not model analog metastability or prove its MTBF.

name: 04_crc_acceptance
title: Only the final correct CRC accepts the 153-byte request
explanation: Before the CRC, position is 152 (0x98): 4 header bytes + 148 payload bytes have arrived. accepted_frames and core_busy are still zero. When rx_valid carries the matching CRC, accepted_frames rises once and mode changes RX(0) → LOAD(1). The board bench also explicitly asserts that a partial header and a complete payload without CRC cannot start inference.

name: 05_load_then_start
title: All 74 inputs are loaded before start
explanation: At the marker, loaded is 74 ones. core_input_index reaches 73 (0x49) with core_load asserted. The controller then drops core_load and pulses core_start; busy rises on the following sampling edge. The core rejects incomplete loads or simultaneous start/load, so no neuron runs on a partial observation.

name: 06_latency_layers
title: Parallel8 inference: 6916 cycles = 138.32 µs
explanation: BUSY and DONE markers are exactly 138,320 ns apart: 6916 clocks at 50 MHz. layer advances 0 → 1 → 2. neuron advances by eight for 16 groups in layer 0 and 8 groups in layer 1; only the first three lanes are committed in layer 2. fault remains zero. done is a level held until a new load/reset/abort, not a one-cycle pulse.

name: 07_rom_bias_mac
title: Synchronous ROM and bias alignment before MAC
explanation: Core states 1/2/3 are BIAS_ADDRESS/WAIT/TAKE; 4/5/6 are WEIGHT_ADDRESS/WAIT/MAC. ROM data updates on a rising edge after address is registered. WAIT prevents use of the previous ROM word. BIAS_TAKE initializes each 40-bit accumulator to signed_bias << 8; each MAC then adds signed_operand × signed_weight. Eight independent bank*.mem files provide eight weights at the same address.

name: 08_eight_lanes
title: Eight accumulators update on the same edge
explanation: At ACC_UPDATE all eight lane accumulators commit in parallel. The accompanying arithmetic table independently checks each after = before + operand × weight from the VCD. MAC repeats every three clocks because WEIGHT_ADDRESS and WEIGHT_WAIT precede each MAC. Parallel8 means eight neurons share one input operand and use different weights; it does not mean eight input samples per clock.

name: 09_relu_group
title: Hidden layer: activate and store eight neurons per group
explanation: After k=73 has been accumulated, state ACTIVATE(7) commits one Q8.8 activation per lane, then neuron changes 0 → 8 and the next group begins. Activation uses arithmetic floor(acc/256), ReLU to zero for negatives, and saturation at 32767 for hidden outputs. The full core regression compares every one of 128 + 64 hidden values against an independent integer model, not just the three final outputs.

name: 10_layer1_transition
title: Layer 0 → 1: correct dimensions and bank offsets
explanation: Before the transition, k=73 and the final group starts at neuron=120. ACTIVATE advances layer and resets neuron. Layer 1 consumes 128 hidden1 values for 64 neurons, with weight_address starting at 1200; layer 2 consumes 64 hidden2 values for 3 outputs, starting at 2232. Bias bases are 1184, 2224, 2296. These addresses refer to each lane bank, not the original unbanked ROM.

name: 10_layer2_transition
title: Layer 1 → 2: correct dimensions and bank offsets
explanation: Before the transition, k=127 and the final group starts at neuron=56. ACTIVATE advances layer and resets neuron. Layer 1 consumes 128 hidden1 values for 64 neurons, with weight_address starting at 1200; layer 2 consumes 64 hidden2 values for 3 outputs, starting at 2232. Bias bases are 1184, 2224, 2296. These addresses refer to each lane bank, not the original unbanked ROM.

name: 11_capture_q88
title: Capture three ordered Q8.8 values before constructing CRC
explanation: CAP0/CAP1/CAP2 read outputs 0/1/2 on successive clocks, giving raw signed [-57, 76, 42] = [-0.22265625, 0.296875, 0.1640625]. All three match golden vector 1. Only after sample2 is captured does result_valid rise and response_valid pulse. response_crc is 0F. safety_permit here means a valid policy residual; this design has no motor-driver enable output.

name: 12_tx_full_packet
title: TX: exactly 11 bytes with independent wire decoding
explanation: The response on the wire is 5A A5 02 06 C7 FF 4C 00 2A 00 0F. C7 FF = -57, 4C 00 = 76, 2A 00 = 42, in little-endian signed Q8.8. Eleven tx_send pulses produce eleven complete 8N1 bytes; received reaches 11. The monitor decodes the pin without reusing the DUT receiver, and independently checks header, numerical results and CRC.

name: 13_tx_exact_bits
title: TX zoom: start, all eight bits and full stop bit
explanation: The 10-bit shift register is {stop=1, data=0x5A, start=0}; shift[0] drives TX. Named markers show the same 0x5A LSB-first sequence as RX. Each bit is exactly 1080 ns. At 50 MHz, the rounded divider 54 produces 925925.93 baud, +0.4694% relative to nominal 921600. The separately recorded nominal-baud audit passes as well; this screenshot uses an exact-divider host.

name: 14_tx_final_stop
title: Do not return to RX until the CRC stop bit finishes
explanation: After the last send the mode progresses TX_START_LAST(8) → TX_END_LAST(9), waits for tx_busy to fall after ten full bits, and only then returns to RX(0). tx_send is one clock wide and TX requires both !tx_busy and !tx_send; this avoids duplicate bytes caused by the registered busy handshake. The stop bit remains high for its complete 54 clocks.

name: 15_estop_immediate
title: KEY1: immediate gating between clocks, then logged once
explanation: KEY1 falls at 1,949,003 ns, between rising clock edges. stop_active immediately rises and all three gated residuals plus permit become zero in the same simulation timestamp; TX returns to idle high. On the following rising edge stop_latched sets; error_code becomes 1, error_flags bit 1 is recorded, and rejected increments once. This is an asynchronous inhibition path followed by synchronous bookkeeping.

name: 16_estop_latched
title: Releasing KEY1 does not restart the design
explanation: Even when KEY returns to 3, stop_latched and stop_active remain high, all residual outputs remain zero, and rejected stays at 1 rather than incrementing each held clock. A new valid packet while latched is not accepted (separate checkpoint at 3,606,192 ns). KEY0 reset is required to clear the latch and fault history.

name: 17_key0_clears
title: KEY0 clears result, counters and history asynchronously
explanation: Before KEY0 assertion the post-reset transaction has again returned the correct result. At 5,522,460 ns KEY0 falls; reset_sync and rst_n immediately clear, permit and all outputs become zero, and accepted/error history clear. A separate held-KEY1 boot case is recorded as a real stop exactly once, rather than mistaken for a clean boot.

name: 18_activation_edges
title: Activation arithmetic: floor, ReLU and output clipping
explanation: Each 1 ns step is an independent combinational activation test, not an inference clock. At the signed 40-bit minimum (-549755813888), hidden output is zero and output-layer value clips to -256. At the maximum (+549755813887), hidden value saturates to 32767 with saturated=1, while the output layer clips to +256. The regression exercises 8364 activation cases before network inference begins.

name: 18b_floor_relu
title: Negative fractions floor before hidden ReLU
explanation: At accumulator=-257 the output-layer result is -2, because arithmetic floor(-257/256)=-2. At -1 the output-layer result is -1, while the hidden-layer result is 0 after ReLU. At accumulator=0 or 1 the scaled value is zero. This proves signed arithmetic floor rather than truncation toward zero. Each test step is 1 ns; it is combinational stimulus.

name: 18c_hidden_saturation
title: Hidden saturation threshold is exact
explanation: With output_layer=0, accumulator=8388607 scales to 32767 without saturation; 8388608 scales to 32768 and is clamped to 32767 with saturated=1. Switching output_layer=1 gives +256 and clears this hidden-saturation flag. Output clipping and hidden saturation are deliberately different operations.

name: 19_bad_crc
title: CRC mismatch rejects without a success reply
explanation: The complete payload has a deliberately corrupted CRC. error_code becomes 6, error_flags gains bit 6, rejected rises once, accepted stays zero, core_abort asserts and all residuals remain zero. No success response is transmitted. This UART protocol bench uses 8 clocks per serial bit (160 ns in simulation); it proves logic/fault behavior, not production 921600-baud timing.

name: 20_framing
title: A low stop bit is a framing error
explanation: The test drives a low stop bit. rx_error causes error 2 and rejection; it cannot be interpreted as a valid data byte or a successful policy response. This UART protocol bench uses 8 clocks per serial bit (160 ns in simulation); it proves logic/fault behavior, not production 921600-baud timing.

name: 21_interbyte_timeout
title: A stalled partial frame is discarded
explanation: A header plus one payload byte is followed by a stall. At the test threshold of 256 clocks (5.12 µs), the parser rejects with error 7, resets position and aborts the transaction. Production uses 1,000,000 clocks = 20 ms. This UART protocol bench uses 8 clocks per serial bit (160 ns in simulation); it proves logic/fault behavior, not production 921600-baud timing.

name: 22_busy_reject
title: Bytes during inference cannot corrupt the active calculation
explanation: A new byte is deliberately received during RUN. Error 9 aborts the in-flight calculation and cancels transmission; no valid residual escapes. This interface requires one complete request/response at a time. This UART protocol bench uses 8 clocks per serial bit (160 ns in simulation); it proves logic/fault behavior, not production 921600-baud timing.

name: 23_result_lease
title: A result expires and the residual gate returns to zero
explanation: The good result is valid first. At the test lease of 100,000 clocks (2 ms), error 11 invalidates the old residual and all three outputs become zero without emitting a fresh successful packet. Production RESULT_TIMEOUT_CYCLES is 1,000,000 clocks (20 ms). This UART protocol bench uses 8 clocks per serial bit (160 ns in simulation); it proves logic/fault behavior, not production 921600-baud timing.

name: 24_inference_watchdog
title: A missing done signal cannot leave RUN stuck forever
explanation: The testbench deliberately forces core_done=0. At the test watchdog of 60,000 clocks (1.2 ms), error 12 aborts RUN and leaves the residual gate zero. This is fault injection, not a naturally observed core failure; production timeout is 100,000 clocks (2 ms). This UART protocol bench uses 8 clocks per serial bit (160 ns in simulation); it proves logic/fault behavior, not production 921600-baud timing.

name: 25_internal_fault
title: An internal core fault also closes the gate
explanation: The bench forces core_fault=1 while RUN is active. Error 10 rejects the transaction and cancels its response. This view is a deliberate fault-injection test of the wrapper. This UART protocol bench uses 8 clocks per serial bit (160 ns in simulation); it proves logic/fault behavior, not production 921600-baud timing.

name: 26_counter_saturation
title: Counters saturate rather than wrap through zero
explanation: The testbench seeds accepted_frames near 0xFFFFFFFF, then completes valid transactions. The counter reaches its maximum and remains there on the next accepted request; outputs still update correctly. Rejected-counter CRC/E-stop saturation and reset recovery are also asserted in the CSV/log. The seeded value is fault-injection acceleration, not billions of transactions run in real time.
